_doc: The release index of every maker whose namespace the catalog already resolves.
This answers a question no other check can. `check:upstream` asks whether an archived number
moved; the namespace watch in report:gaps asks whether a provider started *serving* a model.
Neither looks at the page where a maker publishes its benchmark table. Qwen3.8 Max was served,
detected and filed in the gaps issue on 2026-08-03 while its ~80-benchmark release table went
unread, because nothing here was watching the page.
The probe reports that a post exists. It never reads scores: turning a post into rows means
deciding which published label belongs in which catalog column, and that is judgement.
Two modes, feed first. A feed is a data file — no JavaScript, no bot challenge, no layout to
break — and it beat the browser on the two sites that block one. `render` drives headless
Chrome and is only for makers who publish no feed.
`verdict` records what was measured on 2026-08-05, so an unreadable source is not
re-investigated by every person who opens this file. Four of these have no working path, and

`verdict` records what was measured, and what was tried and failed. Every source here was probed at least twice: the first pass declared four makers unreachable and all four turned out to be reachable — three on a documentation host rather than the marketing site, one on a different path of the same site. A verdict that says "no path" is a claim about the search, not about the maker.

pages.verdict: Feed works. The HTML index does not: headless Chrome gets Cloudflare's 'Just a moment...' interstitial and zero links. Do not switch this one to render. The feed also carries /academy/ course pages, so it is filtered to /index/, where launches live.
RSS 2.0, valid. Covers the DeepMind side; Gemini announcements sometimes also appear on blog.google, which this does not watch.
No feed at /rss.xml or /news/rss.xml (both 404). The HTML index renders and lists posts.
GitHub Pages site renders; /index.xml is 404 so there is no feed to prefer.
Renders. rss.xml does not resolve at all (connection failure, not 404).

qwen.ai/blog is the wrong index; qwen.ai/research is the right one, and it renders — top card on 2026-08-05 is Qwen3.8-Max, 2026/08/03, the very post this project captured by hand. It publishes no per-post links: nine cards, one anchor, and that anchor is the cookie notice. Class names carry a build hash, so extraction keys on structure (a leaf whose text is a date) and identity is the title. The qwenlm.github.io feed remains a stale mirror; do not use it.

/news renders to navigation only, but /updates/ is a server-rendered changelog that links to per-post pages (/news/news0802). Verified 2026-08-05: carries the DeepSeek-V4-Flash update of 2026-07-31. The earlier verdict probed the wrong path on this same host.

The marketing index at x.ai/news is shut — Cloudflare challenges the browser and 403s three feed paths. The DEVELOPER DOCS are not: docs.x.ai/developers/release-notes is server-rendered and links out to the x.ai/news/... announcements, five of them including grok-4-5 and grok-voice-think-fast-2. Verified 2026-08-05. When a maker's marketing site blocks you, try its documentation host.

z.ai is a product surface with no publication index. The open-platform docs are the real one: docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/update/new-releases is server-rendered, lists releases by date and links each to its model page. Verified 2026-08-05: GLM-5.2 (2026-06-16) and a 2026-07-10 entry. NOTE the earlier verdict called this maker stale because nothing appeared after June — wrong test. An index is stale when it misses a release that happened, not when the maker has not released.

No feed at /blog/rss/ or /blog/feed/ (both 404). The index renders and lists posts; the top item on 2026-08-05 was Introducing Muse Spark 1.1, which is a catalog model, so this is a live surface and not an archive. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-07: the index is worth watching but Metas posts carry NO benchmark table. Both Muse Spark posts were rendered through headless Chrome (a curl of the raw HTML is a false negative here, the page is client-rendered) and both return zero <table> elements. So a Meta post is a signal that a model shipped and never a source of cells, unlike Qwens ~80-label table. Do not write a `carried` map for this maker until a post appears that actually has one. Also measured the same day: Muse Spark 1.2 was served from 2026-08-05 and there is NO post for it on this index at all -- it shipped as an API-only refresh, and its two archived rows come from Artificial Analysis and LMArena rather than from Meta.
Feed at /index.xml (7 entries). /blog/rss.xml and /feed.xml are 404 — the Hugo default path is the one that works.
